<interfaces>
<!-- The live bridge schema (VERIFIED by reading a current $TMPDIR/claude-ctx-*.json, RESEARCH §2.1).
     The executor implements the READER against exactly this shape — do NOT invent fields. -->

The bridge file the statusline WRITER (~/.claude/statusline.py, lines 154-165) emits per render,
at `os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), f"claude-ctx-{session_id}.json")`:
```json
{"session_id":"062b51ef-…","remaining_percentage":75,"used_pct":25,"used_pct_raw":25,"timestamp":1782076190}
```
- Context% the daemon reads = `used_pct` (integer). `used_pct_raw` is the unrounded twin.
- `timestamp` = epoch SECONDS (int). Staleness = `now - timestamp > 60` ⇒ stale.
- `tempfile.gettempdir()` resolves to `$TMPDIR` on macOS (NOT /tmp) — match the writer exactly.
- A subagent / brand-new session may have NO bridge file yet (reader must tolerate missing).
- The sibling `claude-ctx-{id}-nudged.json` ({"nudged":bool}) belongs to the compact-nudge chain —
  the discovery glob MUST exclude it (glob `claude-ctx-*.json` then filter out `*-nudged.json`).

How an existing reader treats this bridge (~/.claude/hooks/cco-compact-nudge.js — pattern to mirror):
- rejects any `session_id` containing `/`, `\`, or `..` (path-traversal guard) BEFORE building a path;
- `if (nowSecs - m.timestamp > 60) skip;` — the exact 60s staleness gate;
- tolerates a missing bridge file (fresh session) by no-op.
</interfaces>
</context>

<threat_model>
## Trust Boundaries

| Boundary | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| bridge file → daemon | The `$TMPDIR/claude-ctx-*.json` files are world-readable tmp files written by the statusline; the daemon treats their contents and the `session_id` in their filename as **untrusted input**. |
| session_id → filesystem path | A `session_id` is interpolated into a file path; a crafted id could traverse the filesystem. |

## STRIDE Threat Register

| Threat ID | Category | Component | Disposition | Mitigation Plan |
|-----------|----------|-----------|-------------|-----------------|
| T-19-01 | Tampering | `read_bridge` path build from `session_id` | mitigate | Reject any `session_id` containing `/`, `\`, or `..` before building a path (mirrors cco-compact-nudge.js). Tested: `read_bridge("../evil")` → None. |
| T-19-02 | DoS / Info | `read_bridge` JSON parse of an attacker-writable tmp file | mitigate | Catch `(OSError, ValueError)` specifically and return None — a malformed/oversized/garbage bridge can never crash the daemon or leak a stack trace. NO bare except. |
| T-19-03 | Tampering (stale-data action) | `is_stale` staleness gate | mitigate | The 60s freshness gate is the trust boundary for "is this signal current"; established here, enforced by the daemon loop in plan 03. Tested deterministically via injected `now`. |
</threat_model>
